rows.why: Items 4 (days) and 8 both fit. Item 8 is closer because two rows test zero values (`0s` → 0 and `1d0h0m0s0ms`). The pick accepts zero values, so `0s` parses to 0. The pick also accepts `d`, matching the `2d` row.
Item 5 asks whether whitespace is allowed. The pick allows no whitespace anywhere, so it would reject `  45m\n`. The scenario expects leading and trailing whitespace to be trimmed.

This scenario mixes several questions: empty string (item 2), bare number (item 1), case and spaces (item 5), unknown unit (item 4) and leading zero (item 8). Item 6 is the closest single match because it covers the number syntax in the most rows (`1.5h`, `-3s`, `+3s`, the full-width `３s`). Its pick allows only ASCII digits, so it rejects all of those, as the scenario expects.
No item asks whether one component's count may exceed the size of the next unit up (`90m` vs `1h30m`) when parsing. Item 3 is about unit order and repeats, and item 9 is about formatting.
Item 3 asks exactly this. Its pick requires strictly decreasing units with no repeats, so it rejects `30m1h`, `1h1h`, `1s500ms2s` and `5ms1s`.
Item 7 asks what the maximum is. The pick caps at 2^53-1 ms, which is 9007199254740991, so `104249991d8h59m991ms` parses to that value.
Item 7 covers overflow and going over the cap. The pick returns InvalidDuration when the total is above 2^53-1 or when it overflows, which matches both rows.

Items 9, 10 and 12 all touch this. Item 9 is closest because it decides the printed form. Its shortest-string rule prints 5400000 as `90m` and 90000 as `90s`, but the scenario expects `1h30m` and `1m30s`.

Item 9's shortest-string rule, with ties going to the larger unit, gives `150119987579m991ms` (18 characters, tied with `9007199254740991ms`). The scenario expects the 20-character `104249991d8h59m991ms`.
No item asks whether formatting then parsing returns the same number. Any normalised form from item 9 would still parse back, so answering item 9 does not settle this.
Item 11 asks what formatting does with a value above the maximum. The pick returns a MillisecondsOutOfRange error, which fits an Err whose Display text mentions milliseconds.
